story.what_it_does: HDFC AMC manages mutual funds and earns fees on the money it looks after. Its average assets under management were about ₹8.91 lakh crore in FY26, and nearly all revenue comes from HDFC Mutual Fund.
story.plans: Management says it will keep operating margins in a band of about 33 to 35 basis points of AUM and keep investing for growth. It has not given any AUM or revenue growth guidance, and it expects a non-cash ESOP cost of about ₹79 crore in FY27.
story.moat: The company is large, with a market share of about 11% of industry AUM and about 17.7 million unique investors. It also has an operating margin of about 36 basis points of AUM and a wide set of equity, debt and liquid funds, though market share has slipped from its best levels.

scenarios.story: Record SIP flows and rising industry equity inflows lift AUM, and fees grow in line with it. Margins stay within the 33 to 36 basis point band while revenue keeps growing at about 14%.
signals_to_watch: Industry SIP contributions and equity-oriented net inflows
Operating margin staying within the 33 to 35 basis point corridor

scenarios.story: Revenue grows about 14% a year and margins stay near 35 to 36 basis points. Profit growth looks uneven because of one-time tax items and weaker other income.
signals_to_watch: Quarterly revenue growth versus the roughly 14% recent pace

scenarios.story: New SEBI fee rules (the TER change) and a prolonged market downturn squeeze fees and slow flows. Newer AMCs and fintech channels could take SIP share while management stays vague on the impact.
signals_to_watch: Gross TER impact on the existing book, which management put at 3 basis points
Market share trend, which fell from 11.5% at best to 11.1%
